title: The Fresh Start Effect

scenes.text: Why do you always say “I'll start on *Monday*”?
scenes.vo: Why do we always say, I'll start on Monday?

scenes.text: Scientists tracked gym visits and searches for “diet”
scenes.vo: Scientists looked at how often people went to the gym, and how often they searched for diets online.

scenes.text: Big jumps on: *New Year*, Mondays, birthdays
scenes.vo: Both shot up on New Year, on Mondays, at the start of each month, and after birthdays.
This is called the fresh start effect. Special dates feel like a clean page in a new notebook.

scenes.text:
Old you made mistakes.
*New you* won't.
scenes.vo: They make you feel like the old you made the mistakes, and the new you is ready to do better.
But here's the secret. You don't have to wait for Monday or New Year.
Make today the special day. Call it day one, and start now.

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
to understand your brain better
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes to understand your brain, one byte at a time.

caption:
Mondays, birthdays and 1st January all feel like a clean page. 🗓️ That's the fresh start effect. But you can start your Day 1 anytime.

Comment 'DAY 1' if you're starting something today 👇
source: Dai, H., Milkman, K. L. & Riis, J. (2014). The Fresh Start Effect. Management Science, 60(10).
